title: The tooth that gets the most fillings
author: Dr. Imogen Ashdown
summary: The lower right first molar comes in at six and has the deepest grooves in the mouth. Here is why it fills first.
body:
If you only ever have one filling, it is probably in tooth 30 or tooth 19, the lower first molars.

They come in at about six, behind the baby teeth, so most parents do not know they are permanent. The grooves are deep, the brushing is new, and juice is everywhere.

That is why we seal them.

title: Grinding shows up on the canines first
author: Dr. Lena Vartanian
summary: Flat tips on the canines are often the first sign of grinding, years before anything hurts.
body: Canines are meant to be pointed. When we see flat, shiny tips on teeth 6, 11, 22 and 27, we ask about clenching and morning headaches.

title: When we leave wisdom teeth alone
author: Dr. Rafael Okonkwo-Reyes
summary: Not every wisdom tooth has to come out. These are the ones we watch.
body: If a wisdom tooth is upright, fully through the gum and you can clean behind it, we usually leave it and check it every year.

title: What a cracked tooth feels like
author: Dr. Imogen Ashdown
summary: A sharp pain when you let go of a bite, not when you bite down. That is the clue.
body: Cracks are common in heavily filled upper molars like tooth 3. The pain comes when you release the bite.

title: The spot everybody misses
author: Priya Halloran
summary: Behind the lower front teeth: where tartar builds up fastest and brushes reach least.
body: Turn the brush vertical and use the tip.

title: Sealants at six and twelve
author: Tomasz Wierzbicki
summary: Two birthdays to remember for sealants, and what we check in between.
body: First molars at six, second molars at twelve.
